title: Mid-course synthesis: local coordinates to a smaller embedding
promptMarkdown: Give a proof portfolio for a compact $n$-manifold, $n\ge1$: (a) construct an embedding into some $\mathbb R^N$ with partitions of unity; (b) when $N>2n+1$, use Sard to find a direction of projection that preserves both injectivity and immersion. Define the bad secant and tangent direction maps, compute their domain dimensions, and identify the final topology argument. Illustrate the method on a circle. You may use smooth projective space and the projectivized tangent bundle as constructed spaces; their bundle charts are studied next unit.
hintLadder: Recall why the scalar partition coordinates are necessary.
A killed difference or tangent vector determines a line, not an oriented unit vector.
